solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Repeatedly sail, say, for English port

parts.note: to ply is to sail regularly back and forth over a route
to mouth is to say or utter

explanation.surface: A sailor who keeps making the same voyage is told the destination is an English port.
explanation.definitionFit: Plymouth is a naval and ferry harbour city on the Devon coast in south-west England.

clue.text: Left with severe pain, become weak

parts.note: anguish is severe pain or distress

explanation.surface: Abandoned and in agony, someone loses strength.
explanation.definitionFit: To languish is to lose vigour or fade, growing feeble.

clue.text: Grown-up concealing alternative name for female who knows best

indicators.note: concealing says one piece hides the other inside it

parts.note: grown-up means mature
other means alternative, as in the other way

explanation.surface: An adult hides an alias for a woman who is always right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mother Nature knows best' is a proverbial saying.
explanation.definitionFit: Mother Nature is the personification of the natural world as a wise woman.

clue.text: Barely supporting global organization? That's not right

indicators.note: in a down answer the supporting piece sits underneath the other

parts.note: UN is the United Nations
just means barely, as in just managed

explanation.surface: Giving the United Nations only lukewarm backing is said to be wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Unjust means unfair, lacking justice or fairness.

clue.text: Robust, hard, and stout

parts.note: H is the pencil abbreviation for hard
stout is a dark beer, a kind of ale

explanation.surface: A description of someone sturdy, tough and portly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stout' reads as plump with the other adjectives; it is the beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Hale means healthy and strong, as in hale and hearty.

clue.text: Prepares to commit robbery, as banker is corrupted

indicators.note: corrupted means spoilt or altered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A crooked banker gets ready to rob his own bank.
explanation.definitionFit: A burglar breaks in, forcing entry to a building as the first step of a theft.

clue.text: Starts off filling our crossword in? Concentrate on these points

indicators.note: starts off picks the first letter of each following word

parts.note: first letter of filling
first letter of our
first letter of crossword
first letter of in

explanation.surface: A solver starting to fill in the grid is told where to focus.
explanation.definitionFit: Foci, plural of focus, are central points where attention is concentrated.

clue.text: Shrine I'm having changed for people on island

indicators.note: having changed says these letters are rearranged into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Someone altering a shrine for the people of an island.
explanation.definitionFit: Irishmen are natives of Ireland, an island nation.

clue.text: Frenchman's so long in air over centre of Rouen, disorientated

indicators.note: disorientated means thrown into confusion, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

indicators.note: centre of picks the middle letter of the five-letter town name that follows

parts.note: the middle letter of Rouen

explanation.surface: A Frenchman waves goodbye while flying over Rouen, losing his bearings.
explanation.definitionFit: Au revoir is the French farewell, the equivalent of the English 'so long' or 'goodbye'.

clue.text: Get connected with granny, perhaps? Not from what we hear

indicators.note: from what we hear says the answer sounds like the clue word before it

parts.note: the word not, said aloud

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether to get in touch with granny, and the reply is no.
explanation.walkthrough: A granny is a kind of knot, an insecure reef knot tied the wrong way, so tying one is to 'get connected with granny'.
explanation.definitionFit: To knot is to tie or fasten, and a granny knot is one example of the knot used.

clue.text: Guests in the country who use part — i.e. some, but not all

indicators.note: but not all says only part of the run of words is taken, a hidden stretch

parts.note: the run of letters starts inside who and ends inside some, crossing the words between

explanation.surface: An odd instruction about guests who use only part of something, some but not the whole.
explanation.definitionFit: House parties are gatherings of guests staying for several days at a country house.

clue.text: Obsessive hobbyist giving art up, in strange protest

indicators.note: in a down answer, up says the word is read from the bottom, reversed

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: strange means odd, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A fanatic gives up on art and joins an odd demonstration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns ART into TRA; 'strange' turns PROTEST into SPOTTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A trainspotter collects locomotive numbers, a byword for a nerdish hobby.

clue.text: Novel title brother briefly used for book

indicators.note: novel means new or original, so the letters are made into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
bro is the short form of brother

explanation.surface: A sibling borrowed the title of a novel for his own book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' and 'book' sit together as if both were about fiction; the first is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The book of an opera or musical is its text, which is called the libretto.

clue.text: Bad feeling when leader's removed from platform

indicators.note: leader's removed from says the first letter of the following word goes

parts.note: a podium is a raised platform

explanation.surface: Resentment arises when a leader is ousted from the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Odium is widespread hatred or disgust, a strongly hostile sentiment.

clue.text: Look into big contract for winter sports event

indicators.note: into says one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a slam is a bridge contract to win all or all but one trick
lo is an old word meaning look or behold

explanation.surface: Someone investigates a major business deal for a winter sports event.
explanation.walkthrough: In the card game bridge a grand or small slam is the biggest contract a side can bid.
explanation.definitionFit: A slalom is a downhill ski race weaving between poles, held on snow.

clue.text: Doctor on TV with a way to stop the trots

parts.note: Doctor Who is the long-running BBC science-fiction series

explanation.surface: A TV doctor offers a remedy for diarrhoea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The trots' is slang for diarrhoea, which the surface suggests; really it is a trotting horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Whoa is the command a rider gives a horse to make it halt from a trot.

clue.text: Don't complete Roman building job? That's nothing special

definitions.meaning: first meaning, read as a phrase: Rome wasn't built in a day

explanation.walkthrough: The proverb says Rome wasn't built in a day; the first reading splits the answer into WORK A DAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Workaday means commonplace and ordinary, as in a workaday life.

clue.text: Non-U love match a cause of tears

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

indicators.note: Non before U says the letter U is taken away

parts.note: a union is a match or marriage
taken as the letter U

explanation.surface: A romance across the class divide ends in tears.
explanation.walkthrough: Non-U is British slang for not upper-class; here it says remove U from the match.
explanation.definitionFit: Chopping an onion releases a vapour that makes the eyes water.

clue.text: Like player out of action, switch position and coach

parts.note: off is one position of a switch
a stage, or stagecoach, is a horse-drawn coach

explanation.surface: An injured player changes position and gets a trainer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coach' suggests a sports trainer; it is the old vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor offstage is out of view, not performing in the scene.

clue.text: Fare for Indian in North America, going both ways

indicators.note: going both ways says the same letters are read forwards and then backwards

explanation.surface: Indian food available in North America, travelling in both directions.
explanation.definitionFit: Naan is a leavened flatbread served with curries in Indian cuisine.

clue.text: Confused nobody in harbour

definitions.meaning: second meaning, literal: everyone is out on the water

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom for bewildered is read literally as a fleet with no ship left in port.
explanation.definitionFit: All at sea is an idiom for bewildered; literally every vessel is out sailing.

clue.text: Check with rook initially exposed expert

parts.note: R is the chess abbreviation for rook

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: first letter of exposed
a buff is an enthusiast or expert

explanation.surface: A chess player gives check with a rook, beginning to expose an expert opponent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Check' and 'rook' paint a chess game, but 'Check' is the definition in its sense of rebuff.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebuff is a blunt refusal or snub, a check to someone's advances.

clue.text: Avoid shower, showing character fault

parts.note: to miss something is to avoid it
to pelt is to shower, as rain pelts down

explanation.surface: Someone who skips the shower reveals a flaw in their character.
explanation.walkthrough: The character here is a written letter, not a personality.
explanation.definitionFit: A misspelt word has a letter wrong, a fault in its written symbols.

clue.text: E.g. small pen, we hear, that's used to authenticate document

indicators.note: we hear says the answer sounds like the word given

parts.note: a pen is a female swan, and a young swan is a cygnet

explanation.surface: A small pen is used for signing a document.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pen' reads as a writing tool; it is a female swan.
explanation.definitionFit: A signet is a small seal, often on a ring, pressed to make an official mark.

clue.text: Later idea is dafter, though tenable in part

indicators.note: in part says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A notion that came later is sillier but still partly defensible.
explanation.definitionFit: An afterthought is something thought of only after the main plan, a subsequent notion.

clue.text: Politician wanting nothing extra in tax

indicators.note: extra in says one piece is added inside another

parts.note: to try someone's patience is to tax it
nothing is zero, which looks like O

explanation.surface: A politician who wants no further taxes.
explanation.definitionFit: A Tory is a member of the British Conservative Party.

clue.text: Expel some of you students in serious trouble, also

indicators.note: some of says the answer is a part of the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across these two words

explanation.surface: A threat to throw out students who are in deep trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is hidden twice: in 'you students' and also in 'serious trouble'.
explanation.definitionFit: To oust is to drive out or remove from a position.

clue.text: Labour constituent taking journalist's last question

indicators.note: last picks the final letter of the word before it

parts.note: last letter of journalist
to question is to ask

explanation.surface: A Labour voter in a constituency is quizzed by a journalist who has the final question.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Labour constituent' looks like a voter for the Labour Party; it means one piece of work.
explanation.definitionFit: A task is a single job, one part of the overall work or toil to be done.

clue.text: Makes short work of a poet

parts.note: Robert Bridges was Poet Laureate from 1913 to 1930

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses a poet's output quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: To abridge is to shorten a text, so it literally makes a work shorter.

clue.text: Ordered out, disrupting test in class

indicators.note: disrupting says one piece breaks into the middle of another

parts.note: a trial is a test

indicators.note: ordered means arranged, so the letters of out are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A pupil is sent out for disrupting an exam in class.
explanation.definitionFit: A tutorial is a teaching session for a small group, a kind of lesson.
